summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of Crohn’s disease and recurrent ammonium urate kidney stones was admitted with acute left flank pain and hematuria, consistent with a kidney stone episode. Imaging showed no hydronephrosis or visible stone, but absence of a left ureteral jet supported the diagnosis. He developed acute kidney injury likely due to dehydration, which improved with IV hydration. His pain resolved with supportive care. Potassium citrate was initiated to alkalinize urine and prevent future stones. He remained stable, advanced to oral intake, and was discharged home with instructions to maintain hydration, follow up on labs, and continue preventive therapy. Chronic back pain and tobacco use were noted but did not require intervention during this admission.
problems: Adrenal cortical steroids causing adverse effects in therapeutic use
